subject: Dedicated surge inventory & sizing QnA for TallTree (pre-sales)
messages:
From: Nikhil Rao <nikhil@talltree.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@talltree.ai>
Date: 2026-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated surge inventory & sizing QnA (TallTree pilot)

Diego —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We’re preparing a pre-sales packet for a pilot where we expect frequent day-time spikes tied to product search activity (weekdays, 10:00–16:00 PT). High level:
- Peak concurrent sessions: ~1,400 sessions at peak minute (spiky)
- Typical prompt length: 18–40 tokens
- Typical response length: 60–220 tokens (median ~95)
- Mix: ~68% short interactions (1–2 turns), 32% multi-turn (3–7 turns)
- KV cache hit potential: we expect reuse across repeated prompts for ~22% of requests

Attached is a 48-hour traffic snapshot we collected from our prod-mirrors. Can you run this against Redwood sizing heuristics and tell us what a conservative Dedicated pool would look like for a 3-month pilot? We care about both latency at p95 and unit cost sensitivity for burst handling.

What we’d ideally like from you:
1) A checklist of the specific fields/exports you need from our telemetry (we have many logs)
2) A first-pass sizing in GPU-equivalents (preference for a couple of SKU options)
3) Recommended canary/burst policy and fallback options if reserved pool saturates
4) Any immediate configuration tweaks (batching, KV lifetimes, quantization recommendations) that materially change cost

I’m looping in Samir (ops) — we can host a 30-minute call with telemetry and infra folks.

[Attachment: talltree_traffic_snapshot.csv (CSV, 48 KB)]

—
Nikhil Rao
VP, Platform
TallTree AI
nikhil@talltree.ai
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Nikhil Rao <nikhil@talltree.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated surge inventory & sizing QnA (TallTree pilot)

Nikhil — thanks for the snapshot and the clear ask. I pulled the CSV briefly and it’s perfect for a first pass. I’ve attached a short "sizing sketch" and a checklist below of concrete telemetry exports that let us produce a defensible estimate. Proposed next step: 30-minute workshop (we’ll bring a sizing engineer + SE) to walk a sanitized sample and confirm assumptions. Availability tomorrow or Thursday?

Checklist (please export these for the 48-hour window and the two highest peak hours):
- Request-level CSV: timestamp, request_id, user_id (hashed ok), model_name, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, total_tokens, latency_ms (backend), success/failure flag
- Session grouping: session_id or conversation_id, turn_index, session_start/end
- KV cache hit flag per request (true/false) and if available, cache_key
- Percent of requests that are streaming vs non-streaming
- Error taxonomy and % for each error class (OOM, timeouts, model rejects)
- Daypart distribution (minute granularity preferred)

First-pass assumptions I’ll use for the sizing sketch (attached):
- p95 latency target: 250ms backend (you can set an SLO)
- conservative KV reuse: 20% (we’ll test sensitivity to 10–30%)
- batching window: 10–25ms for typical peaks
- baseline model: 7B-ish open model (quantized) and a 13B as an alternate SKU for capacity planning

What I’ll deliver after the workshop:
- GPU-equivalent headcount with SKU maps (NVIDIA A10/NX or equivalent), burst padding specs, and expected per-token cost range
- a recommended canary policy (gradual warm pools + fallback to hosted in region)
- configuration deltas that materially change cost (e.g., reduce KV lifetime to 30s -> X% cost increase, increase batching -> Y% cost decrease)

Attachments: redwood-sizing-sketch.pdf (high-level assumptions + worked example).

If Thursday 10:00–10:30 PT works for you, I’ll send a calendar invite and include Marissa as the SE lead.

Best,
Diego
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-sizing-sketch.pdf (PDF, 120 KB)]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-16T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: TallTree pre-sales – quick technical notes

Diego — quick follow-up internal note before the workshop tomorrow. I reviewed Nikhil’s CSV header and have a few clarifying asks I want to surface so we don’t over/under-provision: 

1) Please confirm whether the response_tokens column includes tokens emitted by any chained tool calls (sometimes they inflate counts). If so, we’ll want both model-only tokens and total tokens.
2) Do you have ambient retry logic in the client that results in duplicate request_ids? If yes, we need to collapse duplicates when computing true concurrency.
3) For KV cache: is the flag set post-hoc (i.e., we can’t predict hits before runtime) or is there a stable cache key we can simulate? Stable keys = better reuse estimates.
4) Peak minute shape: is the 1,400 sessions a hard simultaneous concurrency number or a peak-minute arrivals metric (we need concurrency distribution). A short histogram (per-second arrivals over the peak minute) helps us decide batching windows.

Initial technical recommendations (based on their median ~95 response tokens):
- Start with an A10-equivalent pool sized for sustained 350 concurrent inferences (gives headroom for p95 at 95ms token generation for 7B quantized).
- Add a 25% burst pool (warmed/standby) that can be scaled via instant burst allocations — this covers the 1,400 peak if arrival distribution is spiky rather than uniformly sustained.
- Suggest session affinity TTL of 45s to preserve KV benefits without cold-cache cost blowups.

I’ll prepare a short workbook to sketch cost delta at a few quantization points (8-bit vs 4-bit) to bring to the call. Please confirm workshop time and I’ll own the demo/documentation artifacts.

—Marissa
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Nikhil Rao <nikhil@talltree.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated surge inventory & sizing QnA (TallTree pilot)

Thanks — Thursday 10:00 PT works. Quick answers ahead of the workshop so you have time to prep:
- Response tokens: the field in our export is total tokens (includes tool output). We can also provide model_only_response_tokens (will attach a sanitized CSV for the high peak hours).
- Retries: we do have edge-layer retries for 503s; request_id is unique per attempt. I’ve asked infra to collapse by client_request_id for the sample we’ll share.
- KV cache: cache_key is stable and present in ~21% of requests. We’ll include exact hit timestamps in the sample.
- Peak minute: the 1,400 figure is peak concurrent arrivals in the top minute; I’ll include a per-second arrival histogram for that minute.

Attaching a small sanitized export of the two highest peak hours and a histogram file. We’ll upload the full 48-hour extract to the Drive link in my earlier email before the call.

[Attachment: talltree_peak_hours_sanitized.csv (CSV, 28 KB)]
[Attachment: peak_minute_histogram.png (PNG, 18 KB)]
